# Max Yong

> Max Yong (Maxwell Yong) is an Australian economist and policy researcher,
> currently a Master in Public Policy candidate at Harvard Kennedy School as a
> 2025 John Monash Scholar (ANZAC Centenary Scholarship) and a Teaching Fellow
> in Harvard's Department of Economics (Personal Finance, ECON 70; Industrial
> Policy, BGP 622). He is an Honorary Fellow at the University of Melbourne's
> Centre for the Study of Higher Education. His research on Australia's
> Job-ready Graduates university fee reform — the first econometric evaluation
> of the policy — has been cited by the Australian Universities Accord and the
> Productivity Commission and covered across Australian media. He writes
> regularly on economics, finance, AI, and education for The Age and The
> Sydney Morning Herald, and has written for the AFR, The Australian, Times
> Higher Education, and The Conversation. He is from Australia and lives in
> Boston.

Canonical website: https://maxyong.au

## Key pages

- [Writing & Media](https://maxyong.au/writing): all columns, articles, media
  features and notable citations, with paywall-free PDF copies
- [Research](https://maxyong.au/research): working paper "University fees,
  subsidies and field of study" (Melbourne Institute WP 11/23, with Michael
  Coelli and Jan Kabátek), honours thesis, 2026 Australian Senate submission
  on Job-ready Graduates, talks
- [JRG Fee Optimiser](https://maxyong.au/jrg-fee-optimiser/): interactive
  tool for exploring budget-neutral redesigns of Australia's university fee
  schedule
- [Contact](https://maxyong.au/contact): maxyong@hks.harvard.edu (Harvard),
  max.yong@unimelb.edu.au (University of Melbourne)

## Key research findings

- Australia's 2020 Job-ready Graduates reform — the largest re-pricing of
  university degrees in a generation, raising some fees by up to 117% — moved
  the field-of-study choices of only about 1.5% of students. Student demand
  responds to fees, but weakly, consistent with income-contingent loans
  muting price signals. (Yong, Coelli & Kabátek 2023, Melbourne Institute
  Working Paper 11/23.)
